arguments.prompt: Create a refined editorial illustration of a small paper workshop, viewed from directly overhead. On a warm ivory desk, two horizontal record cards sit neatly side by side. Each card has a permanent brass identification tab on its left edge, suggesting an identity that stays intact throughout cleaning. Soft graphite smudges and loose paper fibers sit outside the cards, suggesting whitespace that has been removed. The first card holds one complete amber rectangular tile. The second card has a rectangular slot receiving a blue tile from a separate, clearly visible lookup tray above it; a thin blue line connects the tray to the matching slot, making the source of the replacement unmistakable. Below the cards, a simple transparent measuring frame encloses both cards, symbolizing a final check. Use tactile cut-paper collage, delicate pencil contours, subtle shadows, and a restrained palette of ivory, slate blue, amber, and charcoal. Keep the arrangement balanced, precise, spacious, and easy to read. No people, faces, robots, brains, or emotional expressions. No text or numerals. This is a visual metaphor for a verified data-cleaning process, not a depiction of a felt emotional experience. Landscape composition, 3:2 aspect ratio.

response.description: An overhead still life on a cream, textured work surface shows a wooden tray with five compartments of rectangular material swatches in ivory, gray, blue, ochre, and charcoal. Two cream boards with brass clips sit beneath the tray. The left board holds an ochre rectangle fitted within a border; the right has a recessed rectangular opening with a blue rectangle partly covering it. A curved blue arrow runs from the tray's blue compartment toward that blue rectangle. A long transparent ruler or measuring frame with fine tick marks and brass corner fasteners lies across the bottom. A shallow ceramic dish of torn scraps is partly cropped at upper left, larger blue swatches are stacked at upper right, and torn paper, thread, and dark grains scatter along both sides. Warm cream and brass, soft shadows, tactile fibers, and an orderly central arrangement give the scene a quiet craft-workshop mood, with peripheral scraps adding a sense of material handling.

items.evidence: Only craft materials, boards, containers, an arrow, and a measuring tool appear in the overhead arrangement.
items.name: actors_objects
items.value: No people, animals, or other visibly acting characters are present.

items.evidence: Four vertical wooden partitions separate five swatch compartments; a recessed opening and fitted rectangular border appear on the boards.
items.name: barriers
items.value: Physical dividers organize the swatches, while the boards have bounded rectangular areas.

items.evidence: Each compartment contains overlapping cards, and the blue piece covers the upper part of the right board's recess. No explanatory labels are visible.
items.name: information_access
items.value: The viewer can see the workspace from above, but stacked swatches and the blue rectangle hide portions of underlying surfaces.

items.evidence: The arrow curves down from a blue swatch in the top tray and ends with an arrowhead just above the lower blue rectangle.
items.name: event_relationships
items.value: A blue arrow links the blue swatch compartment to the blue piece on the right board, suggesting a transfer or selection.

items.evidence: The tray, both boards, and measuring frame are shown together from above; slight side faces and cast shadows reveal their thickness.
items.name: viewpoints
items.value: One overhead viewpoint presents the objects as a flat-lay arrangement with visible depth from edges and shadows.

items.evidence: The ochre piece fits within the left board's rectangle, while the blue piece sits over a visible recess on the right; there are no checkmarks, captions, or verdicts.
items.name: outcome_presentation
items.value: Two contrasting material placements are shown, without an explicit statement of success, failure, or completion.
